findings.text: MUTATION_RESULTS.killers is empty for MU22/MU25/MU26 although killedByRequirementTest=true; record the actual shared killers (test names, files, labels).
MUTATION_RESULTS 'battery.fails' counts violated checks while 'errors' counts cases; mixed units (e.g. MU01 fails 43 > 16 tests). Document units.
MU07 mutantSalSha256 is not reproducible (crypto.randomUUID in addSymbolReader); use deterministic Ids or record that only behaviour is reproducible.

MU05 and MU07 are killed only by one runner test each in program/tester/E1-f1/runners; neither the 8 shared files nor the runnable part of SafetyTests/test detect them. If these runners are not part of npm run check:software, the regression suite does not protect the lock gating or the exact-500 priority after the next change. Consider adopting the two tests into SafetyTests/test (as was done for MU24).

MU22 is killed only through liveness loss; no test shows that removing the NOT T guard would permit a forbidden transition. The guard's safety function remains undemonstrated; do not cite MU22 as evidence for the attempt-owner property.

limits: Offline stand model only; not IDE Verify/Build, not native CRC, not Target, not hardware.

Full current SafetyTests/test suite could not be executed in the minimal copy (several files need resources outside the copied subset); MU05/MU07 regression-protection statement is limited to the runnable subset (401 tests passing identically on F1/MU05/MU07).
